in_hebrew.name: זכריה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: זכריה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'ה' זוכר' או 'זכרון האל'. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'זכר' שפירושו לזכור, ו'יה' שפירושו אלוהים. השם זכריה מופיע במקרא בספר זכריה, אחד מתרי עשר הנביאים.

in_greek.name: Ζαχαρίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ζαχαρίας είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος זכריה, που σημαίνει 'ο Θεός μνημονεύει' ή 'μνήμη του Θεού'. Στο Χριστιανισμό, το όνομα Ζαχαρίας συνδέεται με τον πατέρα του Ιωάννη του Βαπτίστη, όπως αναφέρεται στο Ευαγγέλιο του Λουκά.

in_latin.name: Zacharias
in_latin.long_meaning: Zacharias est forma Latina nomine hebraeo זכריה, quod significat 'Deus recordatur' vel 'recordatio Dei'. Nomen Zacharias in Ecclesia Christiana antiquitus usurpatum est, praesertim in connexionem cum patre Ioannis Baptistae, ut refertur in Evangelio Lucae.

in_english.name: Zacharias
in_english.long_meaning: Zacharias is a Christian name derived from the Hebrew name זכריה (Zekhariah), meaning 'God remembers' or 'remembered by God'. It is rooted in the biblical tradition, specifically in the Old Testament book of Zechariah, one of the twelve minor prophets. In the New Testament, Zacharias is the father of John the Baptist, as mentioned in the Gospel of Luke. The name symbolizes divine remembrance and favor, holding significant spiritual and cultural importance in Christian tradition.

biblical_reference.note: The book of Zechariah is one of the twelve minor prophets in the Old Testament.

saint_reference.note: Zacharias, father of John the Baptist, is commemorated as a saint in the Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: Zacharias is a biblical name mentioned in the Old and New Testaments. The name Zacharias would have held great cultural significance for the Jewish community during the time of the Old Testament, as it reminded them of God's promise to remember and keep covenants made between Him and His people. The name also demonstrates the belief in God's faithfulness and ability to remember His promises, even amidst the challenges faced by the people.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zacharias holds deep spiritual significance as it serves as a reminder of God's faithfulness and promise to remember His people. It encourages individuals to trust in God's steadfast love and remember His promises, even when facing trials and difficulties. In the New Testament, the name Zacharias is also associated with the birth of John the Baptist, who was a forerunner of Christ and played a crucial role in preparing the way for Jesus. Therefore, the name Zacharias carries a message of preparation, faith, and trust in God's plan for our lives.

historical_references.reference: Zacharias, a priest of the order of Abijah, was visited by an angel while performing his priestly duties in the temple. He and his wife Elizabeth, who was barren, were told they would have a son, John, who would prepare the way for the coming Messiah. (Luke 1:5-24)

Zacharias, the father of John the Baptist, was struck mute by an angel when he questioned how he and his wife could have a child in their old age. God's promise was fulfilled when their son John was born, and Zacharias was able to speak again after writing on a tablet that his son's name was John. (Luke 1:13-25)

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Zacharias has seen a modern resurgence in popularity due to its unique yet classic sound and its strong biblical ties. It is often used in various forms of media and literature to convey a sense of timelessness or religious significance. On social media, it is seen as a unique and interesting name for profiles, especially for those who want to convey a sense of spirituality or connection to their heritage. In literature, it is often used in historical or religious contexts to add depth and authenticity to characters. In film, Zacharias has been used in various productions, such as 'The Shack' and 'The Passion of the Christ', to represent religious figures or to add a sense of spiritual depth to a character.

name_in_real_life.story: Peter Zacharias, a minister in Jerusalem, Israel, shares that their name Zacharias meaning "God remembered" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Zacharias, meaning "God remembers," emphasizes the belief in God's faithfulness to remember His promises and intervene on behalf of His people. It also reminds us of the importance of remembering God in our daily lives and trusting in His divine plan.

Originating in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin cultures, Zacharias has been used for centuries as a name for both religious and secular purposes. In the Bible, Zacharias is the name of two significant figures – a priest in the Old Testament and the father of John the Baptist in the New Testament. Despite its historical significance, Zacharias remains a popular name today, reflecting the enduring appeal of its meaning and cultural associations.
